case.title: Putailai's Zichen anode plant in Malaysia
case.subtitle: Zichen Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. · Gurun, Kedah, Malaysia
case.question: Scanning five export corridors, can Sayari find a Chinese-owned anode maker shipping to the US from a third country?
case.headline: Not yet. In five corridors we found no Chinese-owned anode maker shipping artificial graphite to the US. The rows were electrode makers, machined graphite parts, forwarders and mislabelled chemicals. The one Chinese-owned anode plant in these countries, Putailai's Zichen Malaysia, is clear in the registry: 100% owned through Singapore by Shanghai Putailai. But it is still being built and has no trade.
case.summary_for_non_experts: We scanned US import records of artificial graphite from five countries where Chinese anode makers might set up. None showed a Chinese-owned anode producer selling to US battery plants. The only Chinese-owned anode plant in those countries is Putailai's 50,000-tonne plant in Kedah, Malaysia, which broke ground in June 2026. Unlike Case 1, the registry shows exactly who owns it, so if it ever ships to the US, the ownership question that decides US tax credits will already be answered.

steps.title: Five corridors, no Chinese anode maker
steps.text: Since January 2024, US imports of artificial graphite (HS 3801.10) came from 347 suppliers in Mexico, 107 in Korea, 8 in Thailand, 5 in Vietnam and 2 in Malaysia. Mexico's leaders are electrode makers and chemical firms. Korea's are POSCO and Japanese-owned carbon makers. Vietnam's top shipper sends machined graphite jigs. Thailand's are mostly forwarders.

steps.title: Where 'anode' does show up
steps.text: Searching row descriptions for 'anode' found 398 US-bound rows, none from Vietnam, Malaysia or Thailand. Mexico's and Oman's 'anode' rows are mislabelled chemicals. Singapore is different: 'carbon anode materials' reached General Motors, L-H Battery and NextStar Energy in Aug–Sep 2026 with no producer named. The only named shipper was an Indonesian forwarder.

steps.title: The plant: registered, not yet shipping
steps.text: Zichen Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. was registered on 23 Sep 2025 to make battery materials and carbon products. Press reports put its 50,000-tonne anode plant in Gurun, Kedah, with ground broken on 1 June 2026 and about two years of building ahead. Sayari shows no trade in or out.

steps.title: The owner: in the registry this time
steps.text: Malaysian shareholder data lists Putailai (Singapore) as owning 100% of Zichen Malaysia. Sayari's ownership graph links that company to the Shanghai-listed Putailai group, and Putailai's SSE announcement of 11 Mar 2026 calls Zichen Malaysia a wholly owned overseas grandchild company, while a 2023 announcement calls Putailai (Singapore) wholly owned. One director, Han Zhongwei, shares a name with a listed Putailai shareholder. That is a lead, not a link.

steps.title: A trail that hasn't started
steps.text: With no trade, we can't show inputs from China or buyers in the US. A name search for the group's existing exports returned only unrelated 'Zichen' firms. Two boolean searches returned nothing. The plant is a watch item: its first export rows will show whether its graphite reaches US cell plants.

caveats: Building a plant abroad is legal and common. Nothing here shows wrongdoing by any company named.
US buyers and corridor shippers are named because they appear in customs records; this says nothing about their compliance.
HS 3801.10 is noisy: many corridor rows are mis-coded chemicals, electrodes or machined parts. Supplier counts overstate battery trade.
Facet scans count suppliers, not tonnes. A corridor with few suppliers can still carry large volumes.
Sayari's Malaysian ownership data comes from a third-party shareholder source; stake percentages above the Singapore level were not returned.
Name matches between directors and parent shareholders are leads only.
case.answer: No. The rows from Vietnam, Malaysia, Thailand, Mexico and Korea were electrode makers, machined parts, forwarders or mislabelled chemicals. The one Chinese-owned anode plant found, Putailai's Zichen Malaysia, is 100% Chinese-owned on paper but still under construction.
case.why_it_matters: This sets a baseline: as of Oct 2026, the big third-country Chinese anode plants aren't yet shipping to the US. It also shows that country-level trade totals can mislead, so buyers need plant-level checks.

calls.question: How many suppliers ship artificial graphite (HS 3801.10) from Vietnam to the US since 2024?
calls.result_summary: 5 suppliers. Facets do not name them; supplier-country buckets include KOR, CHN and others because they list every country a supplier is linked to.
calls.interpretation: A thin corridor. Five names is few enough to check one by one.

calls.question: How many suppliers ship HS 3801.10 from Malaysia to the US since 2024?
calls.result_summary: 2 suppliers.
calls.interpretation: The thinnest corridor of the five.

calls.question: How many suppliers ship HS 3801.10 from Thailand to the US since 2024?
calls.result_summary: 8 suppliers.
calls.interpretation: Thin; worth listing every name.

calls.question: How many suppliers ship HS 3801.10 from Mexico to the US since 2024?
calls.result_summary: 347 suppliers; buyer-country buckets led by USA (555). Many supplier risk flags are 'psa_' or sub-tier flags.
calls.interpretation: By far the biggest corridor, but size alone says nothing about battery content.

calls.question: How many suppliers ship HS 3801.10 from Korea to the US since 2024?
calls.result_summary: 107 suppliers.
calls.interpretation: Second-largest corridor; Korea has its own anode industry.

calls.question: Who are the five Vietnam suppliers?
calls.result_summary: Minh Thinh Loi (Da Nang, 30 shipments, latest 24 Jan 2025), HS Hyosung Global Logistics Vina (2), Hyosung TNC (1), Graphite India (1), Samsung Electronics Vietnam Thai Nguyen (1, 2019).
calls.interpretation: No Chinese-owned anode maker. One local parts maker, Korean groups and a logistics firm.

calls.question: Who are the eight Thailand suppliers?
calls.result_summary: Shanghai Supreme International Freight Forwarding, T.C. Pharmaceutical (three records), ECU Worldwide (Thailand), AC Container Line, China Highwin (Thailand), Topasia International Logistics.
calls.interpretation: Forwarders and a drinks maker. China Highwin is the only Chinese-named one; checked further.

calls.question: Who are the two Malaysia suppliers?
calls.result_summary: Graphite India Limited (1 shipment) and PAC Worldwide Corp (1, Apr 2025).
calls.interpretation: No Malaysian producer ships HS 3801.10 to the US in this data.

calls.question: Who leads the Mexico corridor?
calls.result_summary: Top 25 of 347: Carbograf Industrial (220), Syngenta Agro (168), GrafTech Mexico (147), Viakem (94), Carbones Industriales Mexicanos (73), then Dow, Nouryon, Polaquimia, PPG, Mersen and other chemical or consumer firms.
calls.interpretation: Electrode and industrial-carbon makers plus many chemical firms whose rows are probably mis-coded. No Chinese-owned anode maker in the top 25.

params.query: Chinese anode material graphite plant Vietnam OR Malaysia OR Thailand OR Mexico Shanshan Putailai Kaijin Shinzoom Shangtai overseas factory

calls.question: Which Chinese anode makers have plants in the corridor countries?
calls.result_summary: GraphiteHub, Jiemian, Yicai/SSE and Scandasia report Putailai's US$297m, 50,000 t/yr anode plant in Gurun, Kedah, Malaysia: announced 11 Mar 2026, ground broken 1 Jun 2026, about 24 months to build. Shinzoom's planned plant is in Morocco. No Vietnam, Thailand or Mexico anode plant by these firms appeared.
calls.interpretation: Putailai's Malaysia plant is the one Chinese-owned anode plant in the five corridors, and it is not yet built.

calls.question: Do any US-bound HS 3801 rows describe battery anode material?
calls.result_summary: 0 results.
calls.interpretation: The boolean query or the 4-digit HS filter returned nothing. A single word worked later (s518). A finding about the tool.

calls.question: How many Vietnam-to-US shipment rows are there, and who dominates?
calls.result_summary: 35 rows. Minh Thinh Loi sent 30, all to LTD Material LLC. Latest row 25 Aug 2025.
calls.interpretation: One supplier-buyer pair is the whole corridor.

calls.question: How many Korea-to-US shipment rows are there, and who buys?
calls.result_summary: 717 rows, latest 13 Jul 2026. General Motors is among the top buyers (35 rows). Top supplier ID n1lmY6idUXLOGTBCIVO09Q has 129 rows.
calls.interpretation: Korea is a real battery corridor into US plants.

calls.question: Who is Minh Thinh Loi, and who owns it?
calls.result_summary: Da Nang LLC registered 23 May 2007. Legal representative and chairman: Võ Văn Lợi. 23 ships-to and 16 receives-from partners. No shareholder listed.
calls.interpretation: Vietnamese-run parts maker. No Chinese ownership signal.

calls.question: Who leads the Korea corridor?
calls.result_summary: NUC Electronics (129), POSCO Chemical (48), Ibiden Graphite Korea (45), Tokai Carbon Korea (38), LX Pantos (32), Cimilre (32), OEC Global Korea, Futronic, then forwarders.
calls.interpretation: Korean and Japanese producers plus logistics firms. No Chinese-owned producer in the top 12.

calls.question: What do the Thailand rows actually contain?
calls.result_summary: 9 rows. Descriptions include methylsiloxanes, epoxy resin and fruit flavouring. China Highwin (Thailand) has one row on 22 Nov 2024 to Brilliant Group Logistics, described only as 'Graphite; artificial'.
calls.interpretation: Most rows are mis-coded chemicals. Nothing battery-related.

calls.question: What do the Vietnam rows actually contain?
calls.result_summary: Minh Thinh Loi rows (24 Jan 2025) are 'Jig ... made of artificial Graphite' to LTD Material LLC. Hyosung rows are PTMEG polymer. Graphite India sent one row to Antora Energy (25 Aug 2025).
calls.interpretation: Machined graphite parts and mis-coded polymer. Not anode material.

params.query: "anode material" OR "new energy material" OR "graphite technology"

calls.question: Which companies have anode-type names, and where?
calls.result_summary: 0 results.
calls.interpretation: Boolean OR phrases are not handled here. A finding about the tool.

calls.question: Where do US-bound HS 3801.10 rows that mention 'anode' come from?
calls.result_summary: 398 rows. Departures: Germany 68, Singapore 56, Korea 52, China 18, India 11, Bahamas 9, Oman 4, Belgium 3, Mexico 3. None from Vietnam, Malaysia or Thailand. Top buyers include General Motors (78) and Tesla (20); top supplier is POSCO Chemical (86).
calls.interpretation: No battery-anode rows in three of our five corridors. Singapore stands out as a hub.

calls.question: Who ships 'anode' material from Singapore to the US?
calls.result_summary: Of 56 rows, 25 returned. 'Carbon anode materials' went to General Motors (20 rows, 2 Aug – 12 Sep 2026), L-H Battery Company (2 rows, Aug 2026) and NextStar Energy (1 row, 12 Sep 2026), with no shipper named. One row (12 Sep 2026) was shipped by PT. OEC Freight Indonesia to OEC Freight (NY).
calls.interpretation: Battery-grade anode is reaching US plants through Singapore, but the producer is hidden. The one named shipper is an Indonesian forwarder.

calls.question: What are the three Mexico 'anode' rows?
calls.result_summary: Acrylic polymer to Harris Paints (Apr 2025), polyethyleneamines to Complex Chemical (Jul 2024), surfactant to Nouryon (Jan 2023).
calls.interpretation: All mis-coded chemicals. Mexico has no anode trail in this data.

calls.question: Is China Highwin (Thailand) a producer?
calls.purpose: Check the only Chinese-named Thai shipper
calls.result_summary: Only source is US import data. One trade partner: Brilliant Group Logistics. 2 shipments sent in total. No owners or officers.
calls.interpretation: No sign of a plant.

calls.question: Are there other China Highwin records?
calls.result_summary: 13 records. The main one (Thai reg. 0745560004379) carries a US OTI number, 029257, which is issued to ocean freight intermediaries.
calls.interpretation: China Highwin is a freight forwarder. Excluded as a candidate plant.

calls.question: Are the Oman 'anode' rows a Chinese anode plant?
calls.result_summary: 4 rows, Oct–Nov 2024, from B P Refineries (India) to PMC Biogenix, Memphis: erucic acid and fatty acids in ISO tanks.
calls.interpretation: Mis-coded chemicals. Shows how noisy HS 3801.10 is.

calls.question: Does Sayari hold Putailai's Malaysian company?
calls.result_summary: Zichen Malaysia Sdn. Bhd., Malaysian reg. no. 202501044592. Other hits were unrelated Chinese sole traders.
calls.interpretation: One clean record for the plant company.

calls.question: Which record is the Chinese parent?
calls.result_summary: Registry record 上海璞泰来新能源科技集团股份有限公司 (USCC 91310000055944463E; countries CHN, SGP, HKG), an English securities record, and smaller group records.
calls.interpretation: The registry record is the parent; the English one is kept as a lead.

calls.question: Who owns and runs Zichen Malaysia, and does it trade?
calls.result_summary: Registered 23 Sep 2025, Sdn Bhd, office at Menara BHL, George Town, Penang. Purpose: production and sale of advanced battery materials and carbon-based products; import/export. Shareholder: Putailai (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., 100%. Directors: Liu Fang, Han Zhongwei and a third director. Trade count: 0 sent, 0 received.
calls.interpretation: Ownership is in the registry. There is no trade yet.

calls.question: Does the chain reach the Chinese parent?
calls.result_summary: 50 owner paths returned (output saved and parsed with Python). Path: Zichen Malaysia ← Putailai (Singapore) ← 上海璞泰来新能源科技集团股份有限公司 ← Chinese individuals (including 韩钟伟), funds, banks and the national social security fund.
calls.interpretation: Registry-backed chain from the plant to the Chinese listed parent. Percentages above the Singapore level are not shown.

calls.question: Does any Putailai/Zichen company already ship to the US?
calls.purpose: Look for the group's existing US trail
calls.result_summary: 2,987 rows, all for unrelated firms that share the word Zichen (phone cases, brake rotors, hair clips).
calls.interpretation: A name-only query without HS filter is useless here. We could not see the group's China-to-US anode trail.

params.query: "Zichen Malaysia" Putailai Gurun Kedah anode 50,000 tonnes

calls.question: Is Zichen Malaysia the company building the plant?
calls.purpose: Cross-check the registry entity with the company's announcement
calls.result_summary: SMM and Mysteel report that the project is 'undertaken by Zichen Malaysia Sdn. Bhd.'; a post quoting the announcement calls it Putailai's 'wholly-owned overseas subsidiary'. Yicai places the plant in Gurun Heavy Industrial Park, Kedah. The groundbreaking notice lists raw material crushing, granulation, graphitization and carbonization workshops.
calls.interpretation: Registry record and company statement agree. The plant is designed to do the full process, not just finish imported graphite.

calls.question: Who is the first director of Zichen Malaysia?
calls.purpose: Officers linking the plant to its parent
calls.result_summary: Han Zhongwei, with addresses in Pudong, Shanghai (the second is a Zhangjiang industrial address). Sources: Malaysian and Singapore shareholder profiles.
calls.interpretation: The director is Shanghai-based. Putailai is a Shanghai company.

calls.question: Who is the Putailai-group shareholder with the same name?
calls.purpose: Officers linking the plant to its parent
calls.result_summary: 韩钟伟 (Han Zhongwei). Sources: China CNinfo stock-exchange data, China SAIC and company directories. No address.
calls.interpretation: Same name, and the stock-exchange source fits a listed-company shareholder, but there's no shared identifier, so it stays a lead.

calls.question: Who is the second director of Zichen Malaysia?
calls.purpose: Officers linking the plant to its parent
calls.result_summary: Liu Fang, with an address in Pudong, Shanghai. Source: Malaysian shareholder profiles.
calls.interpretation: A second Shanghai-based director. It is a very common name, so the match to the Putailai shareholder stays weak.
